messages.subject: excluding invalid replications
messages.body_plain:
Hi Michael,

I am trying to use MpluAutomation to run simulations. One problem I encounter is inadmissible solution. In such case, Mplus will give warning / error messages. I want to exclude such replications from my summary statistics (such as power, bias, etc.).

Do you know how to exclude such replications in MplusAutomation? These warnings / errors messages are text (not numeric), I am not sure how to make use of them.

Thanks,

Best,
Bo

messages.subject_clean: inquiry on simulation using cov matirix
messages.body_plain:
Hi Sookyoung,

In this case, I would encourage you to use the mean and covariance matrix to simulate data in R that matches the desired structure. There are a variety of tools for doing so, but the mvrnorm function in the MASS package is quite common. Below is an example that I have used in my SEM class taken from Brown's CFA book (Ch. 8), which may give a sense of how to approach the problem.

Best,
Michael

rawdat <- '
1.00
0.78  1.00
0.80  0.77  1.00
0.56  0.51  0.48  1.00
0.52  0.51  0.46  0.78  1.00
0.59  0.51  0.51  0.80  0.79  1.00
0.16  0.15  0.17  0.14  0.18  0.16  1.00
0.19  0.13  0.18  0.14  0.16  0.16  0.81  1.00
0.12  0.17  0.17  0.17  0.20  0.16  0.75  0.80  1.00
0.16  0.13  0.17  0.15  0.16  0.18  0.56  0.52  0.50  1.00
0.16  0.14  0.18  0.15  0.16  0.18  0.51  0.58  0.51  0.81  1.00
0.16  0.15  0.14  0.16  0.16  0.14  0.52  0.57  0.52  0.80  0.79  1.00
'

#standard deviations of variables
sds <- as.numeric(strsplit('1.40  2.10  1.30  2.30  2.40  1.90  2.00  2.90  2.30  3.10  2.20  1.20', '\\s+', perl=TRUE)[[1]])

cormat <- getCov(rawdat)

#this is the covariance matrix to be analyzed
covmat <- lavaan::cor2cov(cormat, sds)

rownames(covmat) <- colnames(covmat) <- c("P1", "P2", "P3", "C1", "C2", "C3", "E1", "E2", "E3", "S1", "S2", "S3")

df <- mvrnorm(n=275, mu=rep(0, 12), Sigma=covmat, empirical = TRUE)

messages.subject: Re: excluding invalid replications
messages.body_plain:
Hi Bo,

What worked for me is to make some if statements.

For example only include replications without errors: if (length(all_output[[outfile]]$errors) == 0)

Here's an example of how to registrate whether there are any warnings regarding the (co)variance matrix not being positive definite, while iterating through the replications [repl]:
warning_pos_def[repl] <- ifelse(length(grep(pattern = "NOT POSITIVE DEFINITE", all_output[[outfile]]$warnings[1])) != 0, 1, 0)
Please not that this function only checks for the term ''NOT POSITIVE DEFINITE'' in the first warning. If you want to check all the warnings, the code should be adapted.

There might be more elegant ways to solve this issue, but this worked for me.

Best,

Jitske

messages.subject: Re: readModel from simulation result
messages.body_plain:
Hi Sookyoung,

SummaryTable is intended to show the summary (global) statistics of multiple models. These are in the $summaries element from readModels(). Example include AIC, LL, and number of parameters.

It sounds like you're interested in the parameter-level statistics Mplus generates from the simulation. These would be in $parameters element of the output from readModels. When in doubt, use the str() command to get a sense of the structure of the output of readModels.

So, I think you'd want something like:

lapply(allModelParameters, function(model) {
  print(model$parameters$unstandardized)
})

Or you could add the model name as a column within the anonymous function and use do.call(rbind, ...) to combine these into one data.frame.

Hope this helps,
Michael

messages.body_plain:
Dear, I am grateful to received a lot of help from Michael and other colleagues on this site. I have one more question and I would like to ask for help. Is it possible to extract summary values ​​(H0, AIC, BIC, etc.) for each replication generated by savedata in the simulation study using mplusautomation ? Manual say that "getSavedata_Data" refers to an output file, not actual dataset generated by savedata.

Best Regards,
Sookyoung Son.
